text:
emily: Heads up — discovered a partner ingestion log that contains a KMS-wrapped blob referencing svc-ingest-prod. Looks like a developer accidentally uploaded a gzipped backup with wrapped ciphertext to partner-s3 yesterday. Not clear if partner downloaded it yet.
raj: Yikes. Do we know which KMS key was used to wrap?
emily: It's wrapped with projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/ingest-wrap (our customer-managed key). The blob filename: ingest-backup-2026-03-22.gz.enc.
olivia: If they only have ciphertext, risk is low unless they have access to the decrypt RPC or someone leaked the key. But we need containment + rotation plan.
mike: Agreed. Immediate steps I suggest: 1) deny decrypt for that key via IAM (add conditional deny for serviceaccounts except specific vault proxy), 2) create a new wrapping key and start rewrap sweep, 3) rotate the service account keys used by ingest, 4) enable transit/audit logs on Vault and KMS for the key.
emily: Can we short-circuit decrypt while we assess? I can push an IAM deny binding for a few minutes. Any objections?
raj: Do it. Post the exact gcloud command here so infra can audit.
emily: Running: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ingest-wrap \
  --location=global --keyring=ingest \
  --member='user:infra-automation@redwood.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' --condition=None
```
(We're going to replace this with a deny binding via org policy — coordinating with infra.)
olivia: Note: that command actually grants. For deny we need an IAM deny policy at the resource level (org policy or IAM deny bindings). If you want immediate block, set key version state to 'disabled' for the current version so decrypts fail.
mike: Good catch. Use: `gcloud kms keys versions disable 1 --key=ingest-wrap --location=global --keyring=ingest` — then rotate to a new version after rewrap.
emily: Disabled version 1. Decrypts should fail now (I can revert after we confirm rewrap path).
sec-bot: ALERT: KMS key ingest-wrap had version state change by emily at 2026-03-23T16:28:12Z. Audit record created (kms.googleapis.com).
raj: Next: rewrap plan. Vault transit can do rewrap if we have plaintext, but we don't. Instead we must treat ciphertext as unrecoverable unless partner returns it. So rotate keys and rotate service-account keys that could decrypt origin plaintext.
olivia: Also update Vault mount policies: move ingest secrets under a dedicated path `secret/ingest/compartment/` with stricter ACLs and revoke legacy tokens bound to the old path. Need to run token-scavenge.
mike: I'll prepare a small playbook:
- Create new KMS keyring/cryptoKey ingest-wrap-v2 (disabled initial version).
- Re-issue new service account keys for svc-ingest-prod and update deploys (rolling update).
- Update Vault transit/rewrap policy to use ingest-wrap-v2 for future wraps.
- Revoke all active Vault tokens with path matching `secret/ingest/*` (token-list -> revoke).
- Enable key access logs and create alert when decrypt attempted from unapproved identities.

(Commands I'll run on confirmation):
```
gcloud kms keyrings create ingest-v2 --location=global
gcloud kms keys create ingest-wrap-v2 --location=global --keyring=ingest-v2 --purpose=encryption
# create new SA key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/svc-ingest-prod-key.json --iam-account=svc-ingest-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# revoke old keys after deploy
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete OLD_KEY_ID --iam-account=svc-ingest-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
emily: Timeline: I'll coordinate partner outreach to ask them to delete the blob and confirm not downloaded. Legal + partner-ops looped. Meanwhile infra, go ahead with the disabled version and key-v2 creation.
raj: For audit visibility, add conditional logs in Cloud Audit Logs and enable Vault's audit devices to stream to BigQuery for a week. We'll run a query for any decrypt/unwrap calls against ingest-wrap.
olivia: Also we should rotate any ingested backup keys stored in Secrets Manager or Vault that could reconstruct plaintext. Run `vault list auth/token/lookup` to find tokens and revoke.
mike: I'll open a short-lived runbook doc and a checklist in the incident tracker. Can someone own the service-account rotation end-to-end?
emily: I'll own SA rotation and partner comms. raj you own KMS and IAM changes. olivia you own Vault ACLs and token revocation. mike you own incident doc + alert creation.
sec-bot: ACTIONS: emily (owner: SA rotation & partner comms), raj (owner: KMS IAM), olivia (owner: Vault ACLs), mike (owner: incident doc).
raj: Quick question — if partner already downloaded the ciphertext, do we need to rekey data at rest for historical restores? That depends on whether plaintext existed elsewhere. We'll plan for a conservative restore plan: assume leak may lead to plaintext if key compromise; create new keys and require re-encrypt for any restores older than incident timestamp.
olivia: Also add MFA requirement for vault token issuance to reduce future accidental uploads. Suggest adding a pre-commit hook in our backup tool to block uploading wrapped blobs to external buckets (simple regex + allowed-buckets whitelist).
emily: Will do a temporary policy: backup tool will fail if target bucket not in whitelist. I'll open PR shortly.
mike: OK let's meet in 20 to confirm done steps. Post updates here.
emily: Partner confirmed they haven't downloaded and deleted the blob. Completing SA rotation now, will post key IDs.
emily: Completed: new SA key id: 0a1b2c3d, old key retired. Updated deploys and rotated secrets in Vault for ingest path.
raj: KMS: new key ingest-wrap-v2 created, IAM tightened (deny for all external identities), old key version remains disabled. Audit logs streaming enabled.
olivia: Vault: moved secrets to `secret/ingest/compartment`, revoked 7 tokens, turned on audit device -> BigQuery. Added policy: `ingest-compartment-only` with strict read/write for deploy service account.
mike: Incident doc updated with timeline and RCA draft. Adding follow-up action: quarterly token sweeps and pre-upload whitelist.
sec-bot: RESOLVED: Incident 2026-03-23-INGEST-LEAK marked resolved by emily.
emily: Thanks team. Postmortem to follow in next 48h with remediation owners and timeline. :thumbsup:
